author: original (NevaIB)
title: Circular functions and their graphs

points.text: Graphs, amplitude and period of sin, cos and tan
Functions of the form a sin(b(x+c))+d and transformations

bigPicture: Sine and cosine repeat, so they model anything periodic: tides, daylight, a Ferris wheel. Every parameter in a sin(b(x + c)) + d has a meaning you can read from a graph.

keyIdeas.cue: Amplitude and period of sin, cos and tan?
keyIdeas.answer: sin x and cos x: amplitude 1, period 2π (360°), range −1 to 1. tan x: period π (180°), no amplitude, vertical asymptotes at x = π/2 + kπ.

keyIdeas.cue: Effect of a, b, c and d in y = a sin(b(x + c)) + d?
keyIdeas.answer: |a| is the amplitude; the period is 2π/b; c translates the graph left by c (right if c < 0); d translates it up, so the principal axis is y = d. Maximum d + |a|, minimum d − |a|.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you build a periodic model from data?
keyIdeas.answer: d = (max + min)/2; a = (max − min)/2; b = 2π/period; then choose c, or use cos, so a maximum or minimum falls at the right time.

keyTerms.def: horizontal length of one complete cycle
the horizontal line y = d halfway between max and min

misconceptions.wrong: sin(x + π/3) moves the graph right
misconceptions.right: It moves it π/3 to the left.

practice.prompt: f(x) = 4 cos(3x) − 1. Write down the amplitude, the period and the range of f.
The depth of water in a harbour is d(t) = 2.5 sin(0.5t) + 6 metres, t hours after midnight. (a) Find the maximum depth. (b) Find the times in the first 12 hours when the depth is 7 m.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
